title: Open-square support criterion with scalar-compatible counit normalization
statement:
Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a commutative condensed ring $R$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $R_T=p_T^*R$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules are internal $R_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; $D(T,R)$ is their ordinary unbounded derived category with the actual derived direct images and inverse images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $D^+(T,R)$ for the full subcategory with cohomology zero in sufficiently negative degrees. For an open immersion use the exact extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. All inverse images below use the canonical identifications of the pulled-back coefficient rings.

Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $c:O\hookrightarrow Y$ be open immersions, put $W=V\times_YO$, and write $b:W\hookrightarrow V$, $a:W\hookrightarrow O$ for the projections [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be the reduced closed complement of $O$. For $M\in D^+(W,R)$ set $B_R(M)=Rj_{*,R}b_{!,R}M$. Let
$$\rho_{R,M}:c^*B_R(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{*,R}M$$
be the open-slice comparison, namely the derived restriction mate $c^*Rj_{*,R}(b_{!,R}M)\to Ra_{*,R}b^*(b_{!,R}M)$ of [def-sfb-open-square-restriction-mates] for the commutative square $j\circ b=c\circ a$, followed by $Ra_*$ of the inverse of the actual open unit $M\xrightarrow{\sim}b^*b_!M$. Let $e_{R,M}:c_!Ra_{*,R}M\to B_R(M)$ be the adjunct of $\rho_{R,M}^{-1}$ under $c_!\dashv c^*$. Then
$$e_{R,M}=\varepsilon_{c,B_R(M)}\circ c_!(\rho_{R,M}^{-1}),$$
where $\varepsilon_c$ is the actual open counit. The maps $\rho_{R,M}$ and $e_{R,M}$ are natural in $M$. If $i^*B_R(M)=0$, then $e_{R,M}$ is an isomorphism.

For any morphism $\varphi:R\to R'$ of commutative condensed rings, write $\operatorname{Res}_T:D(T,R')\to D(T,R)$ for exact restriction of scalars along $p_T^*\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The ordinary direct-image and inverse-image scalar-restriction comparisons, and the extension-by-zero comparison induced by the identical underlying extension presheaf and its sheafification, preserve the specified open adjunction maps and $\rho$. For $M'\in D^+(W,R')$ and any $\mu:M\to\operatorname{Res}_WM'$, after inserting these comparisons one has
$$\operatorname{Res}_Y(e_{R',M'})\circ c_!Ra_*(\mu)=Rj_*b_!(\mu)\circ e_{R,M}.$$
No vanishing hypothesis is required for this equality. No commutation of scalar extension with derived direct image is asserted.

proof.text: Work over the reconstructed section-ring sheaves. The internal/section equivalence preserves underlying abelian sheaves, and its derived pushpull comparisons identify the actual geometric adjunctions and their units and counits. The scalar equivalence likewise identifies exact restriction of scalars. By the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_f$, module inverse image is ordinary sheaf inverse image with its action transported, so is exact. The open extension is the same underlying abelian extension by zero with its transported action; hence its sectionwise model and its specified open adjunction identify with the internal ones. All later equalities may therefore be proved in sectionwise modules and transported back. Since every open subset of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact, $V,O,W$ are Noetherian and every open immersion occurring here is quasi-compact. Thus all the complementary-open and qcqs hypotheses used below hold.

source.place: Tags 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero; 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; internal/section transport by the cited normalization lemmas.

proof.text: For every open $d$, the module open/closed result supplies the actual adjunction $d_!\dashv d^*$ and invertible open unit $\eta_d:1\to d^*d_!$. Both functors are exact. Apply the termwise homotopy adjunction and then adjunction localization: this gives $D(d_!)\dashv D(d^*)$ with exactly the termwise unit and counit, including invertibility of $\eta_d$. We use these normalized derived adjunctions throughout; no new choice of an adjunction on the same functors is made.

source.place: Tag 08FJ, lemma-adjoint-lower-shriek-restrict; termwise normalization as in the cited adjunction-localization statement.

proof.text: For an object $K\in D(V,R)$ choose a K-injective representative $I$. The exact left adjoint $b_!$ implies that $b^*I$ is K-injective. Therefore the underived open-slice isomorphism $c^*j_*I\cong a_*b^*I$ computes a natural derived isomorphism $\beta_K:c^*Rj_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*b^*K$. This is the actual slice comparison: on each site object $E\to O$ its underived map identifies $I(V\times_Y E)$ with $I(W\times_O E)$, with the specified module actions. By the counit equation of the cited open-restriction lemma, the underived isomorphism is the mate of the inverse-image composition comparison under $j^*\dashv j_*$ and $a^*\dashv a_*$, i.e. the underived restriction mate of [def-sfb-open-square-restriction-mates] for the square $jb=ca$. Since $c^*$, $b^*$ are exact and $Rj_*$, $Ra_*$ are computed on the K-injectives $I$, $b^*I$, the derived mate of that definition at $K$ is $\beta_K$; in particular it is invertible. Specialize to $K=b_!M$ and define $\rho_M=Ra_*(\eta_{b,M}^{-1})\circ\beta_{b_!M}$. This proves that the isomorphism in the statement exists with its prescribed normalization. Naturality follows from naturality of $\beta$ and $\eta_b$, rather than from objectwise choices of resolutions.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism, and sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize; derived.tex Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives.

proof.text: For the specified $c_!\dashv c^*$ adjunction, the inverse Hom bijection sends $t:A\to c^*B$ to $\varepsilon_{c,B}\circ c_!(t)$. Indeed the transpose of this composite is $c^*(\varepsilon_{c,B})\circ c^*c_!(t)\circ\eta_{c,A}=c^*(\varepsilon_{c,B})\circ\eta_{c,c^*B}\circ t=t$ by naturality of $\eta_c$ and the triangle identity. Taking $A=Ra_*M$, $B=Rj_*b_!M$ and $t=\rho_M^{-1}$ proves the asserted formula for $e_M$. The naturality equation for $\rho$ and naturality of $\varepsilon_c$ give naturality of $e$ by this formula.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint; the inverse-adjunct formula is written out using the specified derived triangle identities.

proof.text: Assume $i^*B=0$ for $B=Rj_*b_!M$. Exactness of $i^*$ gives $i^*H^n(B)=0$ for every $n$. Apply the actual sheaf localization sequence $0\to c_!c^*N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{c,N}}N\to i_*i^*N\to0$ to $N=H^n(B)$. It says that $\varepsilon_{c,H^n(B)}$ is an isomorphism. Exactness of $c_!,c^*$ and the termwise counit normalization identify this map with $H^n(\varepsilon_{c,B})$. Thus the derived counit is a quasi-isomorphism, hence invertible. Since $c_!(\rho_M^{-1})$ is invertible too, the formula in step 4 proves that $e_M$ is invertible. This uses the support hypothesis only here.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; Tags 09BM and 09BN for exactness and open restriction.

proof.text: For $\varphi:R\to R'$, the coefficient square $\varphi_S\alpha_f^R=\alpha_f^{R'}f^{-1}\varphi_T$ follows from naturality of the pulled-back coefficient identifications. Apply the ring-sheaf change-adjunction theorem to each geometric map in the square. It gives the canonical isomorphisms $\operatorname{Res}_Sf_{R'}^*\cong f_R^*\operatorname{Res}_T$ and $\operatorname{Res}_TRf_{*,R'}\cong Rf_{*,R}\operatorname{Res}_S$, compatible with the actual derived adjunction bijections. The internal/section scalar and pushpull normalization lemmas carry precisely these comparisons to the internal categories. The theorem allows arbitrary ring maps: no assertion that restriction of scalars preserves injectives is used.

source.place: Tags 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; 07A6, lemma-adjoint. Apply to the two ringed-topos factorizations through the coefficient maps.

proof.text: For an open $d:S\hookrightarrow T$, compare $d_{!,R}\operatorname{Res}_S$ and $\operatorname{Res}_Td_{!,R'}$ before deriving. On a site object mapping into $S$ the extension presheaf has the same section group on both sides; otherwise both values are zero. The $R_T$-action on either side is the $R'_T$-action composed with $\varphi_T$. Their abelian sheafifications, and the induced actions on them, are identical. The open unit on an object over $S$ is the identity; the counit is induced by the section map into the target module. These formulas are unchanged by restricting scalars, so the comparison preserves both specified maps. Since all functors in these open squares are exact, termwise application and adjunction localization give the same assertions in the derived categories, for arbitrary derived arrows.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, its sectionwise construction and Hom formula; Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; localized using the cited exact-functor and adjunction lemmas.

proof.text: To check scalar compatibility of $\beta$, use its mate description. The open base-change map $\gamma:j^*c_!\xrightarrow{\sim}b_!a^*$ is the sectionwise extension-by-zero identification, with its prescribed open-unit normalization. On K-injectives the mate of $\gamma^{-1}$ through $c_!\dashv c^*$, $j^*\dashv Rj_*$, $b_!\dashv b^*$ and $a^*\dashv Ra_*$ is $\beta$: its underived evaluation is the same fibre-product identification of step 3, and the slice-counit equation specifies its geometric adjunct. Steps 6 and 7 preserve all four adjunction bijections and the sectionwise map $\gamma$, since its coefficient square identifies the same sections with the same action. Mate pasting therefore identifies $\operatorname{Res}(\beta_{R'})$ with $\beta_R\operatorname{Res}$ under these comparisons. Step 7 also preserves the actual $\eta_b$; hence the formula $\rho=Ra_*(\eta_b^{-1})\circ\beta_{b_!(-)}$ gives scalar compatibility of $\rho$. This checks the maps, including their units, rather than only their endpoints.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change (exchange via the actual counits); underived slice normalization from proetale.tex Tag 09A5 and open extension from sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI. Mate pasting is the cited general categorical tool.

proof.text: Write $A_R=Ra_{*,R}$ and $B_R=Rj_{*,R}b_{!,R}$. After all comparisons, step 8 and naturality imply, for $\mu:M\to\operatorname{Res}_WM'$, $$c^*B_R(\mu)\circ\rho_{R,M}^{-1}=\operatorname{Res}_O(\rho_{R',M'}^{-1})\circ A_R(\mu).$$ Indeed apply naturality of $\rho_R$ to $\mu$ and replace its value on $\operatorname{Res}M'$ by the restricted $\rho_{R',M'}$. Under $c_!\dashv c^*$ the transpose of $B_R(\mu)\circ e_{R,M}$ is the left side of this equation. By preservation of the actual open adjunction maps (step 7), the transpose of $\operatorname{Res}_Y(e_{R',M'})\circ c_!A_R(\mu)$ is the right side. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves exactly the displayed mixed-coefficient equality in the statement. The proof uses no vanishing and no scalar-extension/direct-image interchange.

lean.note: Canonical maps are real constructions: rho is the recorded derived restriction mate followed by the inverse of the actual open unit, and e is its inverse adjunct.
